newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-U.S. interest in U.Utilities plant.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-U.S. interest in U.Utilities plant.

text.p: British multi-utility United Utilities has had interest from U.S. companies in its generation plant which it aims to sell by March 1997, chief executive Brian Staples told Reuters on Thursday.
"We have got tremendous interest in the generating assets...quite a lot is U.S.," he said in a telephone interview.
The generating assets were acquired when North West Water took over regional electricity company Norweb last year to form United Utilities.
Staples said United had decided to sell the assets because they were "neither nothing nor something."
He said there were not enough assets to give the benefit of integration into the supply business but there was little opportunity to buy more to build up a useful portfolio.
The assets could be sold to a party which might either treat them as a trade investment or could add them to an existing portfolio.

Staples said United Utilities needed to grow its non-core businesses in order to maintain shareholder value as price reviews in 1999 for electricity and water could curb the growth of earnings in its core activities.
He said the focus would be on its Vertex services business and a new company to be set up in the second half to compete in liberalised energy markets after 1998.
"It is very much a case of getting (the two companies) well positioned, well resourced," he said.
He said part of the moves would aim to have the value of these companies recognised within United Utilities, adding that he would have "some reluctance" to seek separate listings for them.
"It is a step that is too early and maybe too far," he said.

United Utilities turned in pretax profits for the six months to September 30 of 223.9 million stg, up from 167 million stg, and paid out an interim dividend of 12 pence per share, up from 9.27 pence previously.
The company said it intended to make a further initiative to share benefits of outperformance in the second half, but Staples said it was "too early to say" what form this might take.
He said the company was not contemplating any more acquisitions in the electricity sector.
"No, I do not think so. I think we are well positioned as we are," he said.
